$comment: BillieWeather / FinRx logical finance model. Single source of truth for enums and semantics shared by PostgreSQL (Rails, app/models/finance/domain.rb reads this file) and SQLite (clients/universal, packages/finance-core/src/ledger/domain.ts imports it). Physical schemas may differ; semantics may not. Contract tests: packages/finance-core/test/ledger.test.ts and test/services/finance/domain_contract_test.rb.

legacy_account_kinds.$comment: Existing vocabularies mapped onto account_types. Web finance_bank_accounts.kind: cash|credit|unknown. Local statements.account_kind: checking|savings|credit_card|loan|unknown.

income_expense_rule: Income = sum(amount) over kind=income. Expenses = -sum(amount) over kind in (expense, refund); a refund (positive) reduces spending in its category. Excluded and deleted rows never count. The sign of an amount alone never decides income or expense.

link_types.transfer: Money moved between two of the person's accounts. from = outflow leg (negative), to = inflow leg (positive). Same currency: from.amount + to.amount = 0.
link_types.card_payment: A payment from an asset account to a liability account (credit card, loan). Same balancing rule as transfer.
link_types.refund_of: from = the refund (positive), to = the original expense (negative). amount = cents covered. Sum of refunds of one expense <= |expense amount|.
link_types.duplicate_of: from = a row a person or rule confirmed is the same economic event as to (kept for audit; the duplicate is excluded).
link_types.pending_to_posted: from = pending entry, to = posted entry.

kind_inference.$comment: Applied to imported rows only (manual entries carry an explicit kind). Patterns are case-insensitive, Unicode, tested against the ORIGINAL description. card_payment_patterns apply to money IN on a liability account; card_payment_outflow_patterns to money OUT of an asset account (stricter, so 'COMCAST AUTOPAY' stays an expense). Person-to-person transfers (Zelle, 微信转账) are not own-account transfers and stay income/expense. Cases: packages/finance-core/fixtures/kind-cases.json.
rules: liability account, amount > 0: card_payment if a card_payment pattern matches, else refund
liability account, amount < 0: expense (transfer if a transfer pattern matches)

asset/other account, amount > 0: card_payment if 'payment thank you' / 'payment received' (a card statement exported without an account type), refund if a refund pattern matches, transfer if a transfer pattern matches, else income
asset/other account, amount < 0: card_payment if a card_payment_outflow pattern matches, transfer if a transfer pattern matches, else expense
kind_inference.categorized_rule: kindForCategorized: category 'Transfers' -> card_payment if inferKind says card_payment else transfer; category 'Income' or an income-kind category -> income (any sign); amount 0 -> ignored; amount < 0 -> expense; amount > 0 with 'Uncategorized' -> income if inferKind says income else refund; amount > 0 with any other category -> refund.

dedupe.$comment: Account-scoped. Same algorithm as packages/finance-core/src/universal/relations.ts markDuplicates; Rails port app/services/finance/duplicate_detector.rb. Cases: packages/finance-core/fixtures/dedupe-cases.json.
steps: date + amount + normalized description with occurrence counting (an overlapping file's rows match; two genuine identical purchases are both kept)
near match: same date + amount + same merchant key, different description -> review
dedupe.null_account: A match that exists only because one side has no account (legacy rows) is never an automatic duplicate: it becomes possible_duplicate with vars.unknownAccount=1, and the suggested decision is 'include'. Two rows with the same known account, or both without an account, follow the normal steps.
dedupe.description_key: NFKC, lower case, whitespace collapsed, trimmed
